title: Use Absence to Increase Respect and Honor
coreMove: Withdraw before familiarity cheapens you and return when presence has regained weight
sourcePressure: Chapter 16 is supported here primarily by the frozen title and grouped secondary summaries: absence, scarcity, and reduced overexposure can increase perceived value, respect, and honor. The mechanism should stay narrow. Constant availability can cheapen attention, while selective withdrawal can make presence matter more. The chapter should not drift into generic ghosting advice or universal neglect. The supported frame is about managing overfamiliarity, saturation, and perceived rarity. Keep the chapter grounded in attention economics, respect loss through overpresence, and the limit that absence can also damage trust if used crudely or too long. Avoid invented court stories or unsupported historical specifics. Frozen sidecar provides no traceable named anecdote for this chapter; do not fabricate named source anchors.
